```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(usdata)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 14))

data(county_complete)
county_health <- county_complete |>
  select(
    state, name, fips, pop = pop_2019, uninsured = uninsured_2019,
    poverty = poverty_2019, median_income = median_household_income_2019,
    per_capita_income = per_capita_income_2019,
    unemployment = unemployment_rate_2019, bachelors = bachelors_2019,
    hs_grad = hs_grad_2019, median_age = median_age_2019,
    broadband = household_has_broadband_2019, density = density_2010
  ) |>
  as_tibble()
```

# Part A: Two criteria, one dataset (11:40-12:10)

## A1. Build the complete-case data and the full model

`step()` compares models on the same rows, so drop rows with any missing
candidate first. How many counties survive?

```{r}
#| eval: false
ch <- county_health |>
  drop_na(uninsured, poverty, median_income, per_capita_income,
          unemployment, bachelors, hs_grad, median_age, broadband, density)

full <- lm(uninsured ~ poverty + median_income + per_capita_income +
             unemployment + bachelors + hs_grad + median_age +
             broadband + density, data = ___)
nrow(ch)
```

**How many of the 3,142 counties are we analyzing, and which single variable
causes most of the loss?** (Hint: `colSums(is.na(county_health))`.) ...

## A2. Backward AIC and backward BIC

The only difference is the penalty `k`: 2 for AIC, `log(n)` for BIC.

```{r}
#| eval: false
sel_aic <- step(full, direction = "backward", trace = 0)
sel_bic <- step(full, direction = "backward", k = ___, trace = 0)

formula(sel_aic)
formula(sel_bic)
```

## A3. Compare the selected sets

**Which predictors do the two criteria agree on? Which variable(s) do they
disagree about, and why does the criterion with the larger penalty drop
more?** (One or two sentences; mention what BIC's penalty is per parameter
when n is about 1,266.) ...

Refit the BIC choice explicitly (write the formula out yourself; this is what

population.
